UC San Diego Health is proud to be a four-time Magnet-designated organization and has now earned Magnet with Distinction from the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). Magnet is the gold standard for nursing excellence, achieved by only about 10% of hospitals worldwide. Magnet with Distinction is awarded to the highest-performing Magnet organizations, with only a select few earning this prestigious honor. This recognition reflects our commitment to transformational leadership, professional nursing excellence, innovation, exceptional patient outcomes, and an empowering practice environment where nurses thrive.

Are you a compassionate leader ready to make an impact in a dynamic specialty setting? We’re looking for a dedicated Assistant Nurse Manager to join our Gastroenterology team, where you'll play a vital role in both clinical care and administrative leadership.

In this position, you will supervise a skilled team of Registered Nurses and Endoscopy Technicians, ensuring high-quality patient care and efficient daily operations. This role offers a balanced blend of hands-on clinical responsibilities and administrative oversight, providing opportunities to mentor staff, support process improvement, and contribute to departmental excellence.
Join us in delivering outstanding GI care while advancing your nursing leadership career in a collaborative, patient-centered environment.

The Assistant Nurse Manager is involved in ensuring optimal patient outcomes through effective leadership and/or provision of patient care delivery in assigned nursing area(s). Promotes environment for a shared voice in nursing practice and exchange of ideas to continually improve nursing and patient care outcomes. Accountable for the quality, safety, and cost-effectiveness of patient care. Consults and collaborates with other health care professionals to coordinate the management of patient care. Serves as a resource to staff, physicians, students and others.

Supervises staff involved in providing clinical patient care. Assists in ensuring the quality of patient care delivery in a specific patient care area and serves as a role model for professional nursing practice. Assists with the administration and management of personnel, fiscal, and material resources. May assume full responsibility for the unit in delegated areas and in the absence of the manager.
While not required, a cover letter is highly recommended when applying to this position.
Strong verbal and written communication skills for professional effective information exchange with all levels of management, staff, consultants and outside agencies.
Demonstrated hospital management skills, with progressive expertise in patient care services.
Knowledge to manage disaster incidents, sentinel events and ability to problem solve with critical thinking skills.
Knowledge of relevant healthcare information technology and patient care workflows and processes.
Proven knowledge of relevant regulatory requirements, as well as related legislative, accreditation, licensing and compliance environments.
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to quickly analyze problems, determine appropriate level of intervention, and develop and apply effective solutions.
